name: Naturalisation par décret

requirements.blocker_text: This requires 5 years of habitual residence in France.

This requires French at CEFR B2, at both oral AND written level (all four skills — listening, reading, speaking, writing — must independently reach B2, not just an average). This is a NEW requirement effective 1 January 2026, raised from B1.
requirements.fix_path: Prepare for and pass an approved test (TCF IRN or DELF B2) covering all four language skills at B2.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires passing a new civic knowledge examination (examen civique), a formal test distinct from and in addition to the traditional assimilation interview, introduced as part of the January 2026 reform.
requirements.fix_path: Prepare for and pass the examen civique.

requirement_groups.name: Completed 2+ years of French higher education

requirements.blocker_text: This requires 2 years of habitual residence in France, reduced from the standard 5 years, for those who have completed at least 2 years of higher education in France.
This requires French at CEFR B2 (oral and written), same standard as the general route since 1 January 2026.
requirements.fix_path: Prepare for and pass an approved test at B2.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires passing the examen civique, same as the general route.
requirements.fix_path: Prepare for and pass the examen civique.

evidence_required.document: TCF IRN or DELF B2 certificate covering all four language skills, passed in a single in-person session

sources.title: Légifrance — Loi n° 2024-42 du 26 janvier 2024 pour contrôler l'immigration et améliorer l'intégration
Légifrance — Décret n° 2025-648 du 15 juillet 2025 and Arrêté du 22 décembre 2025 (B2 language level, examen civique)
Légifrance — Code civil, naturalisation provisions including the reduced-residence higher-education case

notes: MAJOR LIVE POLICY EVENT, confirmed and already in force at this verification date: French language requirement for naturalisation rose from B1 to B2 (all four skills independently, not an average) effective 1 January 2026, per décret n° 2025-648 (15 July 2025) and arrêté du 22 décembre 2025, implementing loi n° 2024-42 (26 January 2024, the 'loi Darmanin'). A NEW civic examination (examen civique) was introduced alongside this, distinct from the pre-existing assimilation interview — genuinely two new hurdles stacked on the same reform, not just a language change. Any source describing France's naturalisation language requirement as B1 is now stale as of this verification. This mirrors the broader European pattern seen elsewhere in this dataset (Portugal's naturalisation clock doubling, Germany's fast-track abolition, Spain's various reforms) of European countries tightening citizenship access in 2025-2026 — France's version is specifically a language/testing tightening rather than a residence-period change, a genuinely different lever from most peer countries in this dataset. The B2 requirement also applies to marriage-based naturalisation (see fr_declaration_mariage), and CEFR levels for OTHER French statuses are tiered distinctly: A2 for the standard pluriannual card, B1 for carte de résident, B2 for citizenship — worth surfacing this full ladder in any comparison view, similar to how Portugal's descent-route language levels are pending regulation.
